title: Webhook verifier adversarial attack matrix (issue #24)
provenance: Executed by TestAttackMatrix in verify_test.go. Every case is really run against the Go verifiers; 'expect' is the required outcome. Secrets are the synthetic clearly-fake credentials from the golden fixtures.

expect_values.accept: verifier must return nil (control cases proving the happy path is not over-tightened)
expect_values.reject: verifier must return a 401-class application error (fail-closed)
expect_values.accept-with-warn: verifier returns nil AND emits a structured residual-risk warning (Africa's Talking, allowlist unconfigured)

cases.attack: control: golden vector signed with the configured token
signature computed with an attacker-chosen token not in the configured list
body substituted after signing (valid signature, different form body)
signature replayed against a different body
X-Twilio-Signature header absent
no auth tokens configured (misconfiguration must fail closed, never open)
signature header is not valid base64
body differs from the signed bytes by a trailing newline only
valid external signature evaluated against the internal/proxy URL (URL-reconstruction pitfall)
non-form (JSON) body signed by concatenation with the real token; verifier form-parses so the signed payloads differ
control: golden vector signed with the configured app secret
signature computed with a different app secret
body substituted after signing
signature replayed against a different body
X-Hub-Signature-256 header absent
empty app secret configured (HMAC with empty key must never become an open path)
digest contains non-hex bytes
digest truncated (wrong MAC length)
legacy sha1 scheme marker in the 256 header
body differs from the signed bytes by a trailing newline only
control: same MAC encoded uppercase — proves raw-byte constant-time compare, not hex-string compare
MAC with first byte corrupted
MAC with last byte corrupted (same rejection class as first-byte — compare is position-independent)
control: peer inside configured allowlist (AT signs nothing — allowlist is the only control)
peer outside configured allowlist
peer-identity header absent while allowlist configured
peer-identity header unparseable while allowlist configured
allowlist entry has host bits set; entry disabled, delivery rejected
forged XFF leftmost entry claiming an allowed IP — DISCARDED under the rightmost-entry trust model (client-asserted entries cannot fake membership behind an appending edge)
allowlist not configured: accepted WITHOUT verification but a structured residual-risk warning must be emitted
